passage: Essay type: Opinion (To what extent do you agree or disagree?)
question:
Write about the following topic:

Some people believe that the main purpose of a university education is to prepare students for employment.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
It is often argued that universities exist primarily to equip young people with the skills they need for the job market. While I accept that employability is an important function of higher education, I disagree that it should be regarded as its main purpose.

Admittedly, there are strong reasons why career preparation matters. Most students invest a great deal of time and money in their degrees, often taking on substantial loans, and they reasonably expect a return in the form of a well-paid job. Furthermore, modern economies depend on a supply of highly trained professionals, such as engineers, doctors and data analysts, and universities are the only institutions capable of producing them in sufficient numbers. In this sense, degrees in medicine or law are clearly designed with specific occupations in mind.

However, reducing university education to job training overlooks its broader value. Firstly, higher education develops critical thinking, the ability to evaluate evidence and to construct a logical argument. These capacities are useful at work, but they are equally essential for citizens who must make informed decisions in a democracy. Secondly, universities are centres of research, where knowledge is pursued for its own sake. Many discoveries that later proved commercially valuable, such as the principles behind modern computing, originated in research with no obvious practical application. Finally, the job market changes so rapidly that narrowly vocational training may become outdated within a few years, whereas the habit of independent learning lasts a lifetime.

In conclusion, although universities should certainly help students to find employment, their fundamental purpose is to cultivate knowledgeable, adaptable and critical thinkers. Preparing graduates for work is best seen as a valuable consequence of this aim rather than the aim itself.

question:
Write about the following topic:

Some people think that children should start formal education at the age of four, while others believe they should not start school until they are seven.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
The age at which children should begin formal schooling is a matter of considerable debate. Some argue that an early start at four gives children an advantage, whereas others believe that waiting until seven is more beneficial. In my view, a later start, combined with high-quality play-based pre-school, is the better option.

Supporters of early schooling make several valid points. Young children absorb information remarkably quickly, so introducing basic literacy and numeracy at four may give them a head start. In addition, early education can be particularly valuable for children from disadvantaged families, who may have fewer books or learning opportunities at home. Starting school early also allows parents to return to work, which can improve a family's financial situation.

On the other hand, those who favour a later start argue that four-year-olds are not developmentally ready for structured lessons. At this age, children learn most effectively through play, exploration and social interaction, and forcing them to sit still and complete written tasks may cause frustration and even a lasting dislike of learning. Interestingly, several countries with high educational standards do not begin formal reading instruction until the age of six or seven, yet their students perform very well by adolescence. This suggests that any early advantage tends to disappear over time.

Personally, I believe the second view is more convincing, but only if young children have access to good pre-school education. A nursery environment that encourages curiosity, language development and cooperation can provide the benefits of early learning without the pressure of formal teaching.

In conclusion, although early schooling has some merits, a later start supported by play-based learning offers children a healthier and more effective foundation.

passage: Essay type: Problem and solution
question:
Write about the following topic:

Traffic congestion is becoming a serious problem in many major cities around the world.

What are the causes of this problem? What measures could be taken to solve it?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
In many of the world's largest cities, roads are increasingly clogged with vehicles, leading to long delays, air pollution and frustration for residents. This essay will examine the main causes of this problem and suggest some practical solutions.

The most fundamental cause is rapid urbanisation. As people move to cities in search of employment, the number of commuters rises far faster than road capacity can be expanded. At the same time, rising incomes mean that car ownership has become affordable for a much larger proportion of the population, and many people regard a car as a symbol of status as well as convenience. A further cause is inadequate public transport. Where buses are unreliable and train networks are limited, residents have little choice but to drive. Finally, poor urban planning, particularly the separation of residential areas from business districts, forces people to travel long distances every day.

Several measures could help to address these issues. The most effective solution is to invest heavily in fast, frequent and affordable public transport, such as metro systems and dedicated bus lanes, so that it becomes a genuinely attractive alternative to driving. This could be combined with financial disincentives for car use, for example congestion charges in city centres, which have successfully reduced traffic in several European cities. In the longer term, governments should encourage mixed-use development, where homes, offices and shops are located close together, reducing the need to commute. Employers can also contribute by allowing flexible working hours or remote work, which spreads travel more evenly throughout the day.

In conclusion, traffic congestion results from a combination of population growth, rising car ownership and poor planning. Tackling it requires a coordinated approach that makes alternatives to driving both convenient and economically sensible.

passage: Essay type: Advantages and disadvantages
question:
Write about the following topic:

An increasing number of employees now work from home for some or all of the week.

Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Over the past decade, and particularly in recent years, remote working has become a normal part of life for millions of employees. Although this arrangement has some drawbacks, I believe its advantages are more significant.

The benefits for employees are considerable. Most obviously, working from home eliminates the daily commute, which can save several hours a week as well as considerable expense. This time can be spent with family, on exercise or simply resting, which improves overall wellbeing. Remote work also gives people greater flexibility to organise their day, for instance by starting earlier in order to collect children from school. For employers, too, there are advantages: companies can reduce office costs and recruit talented staff who live far away from the head office.

Nevertheless, there are genuine disadvantages. Many people who work from home report feelings of isolation, as they miss the informal conversations and social contact of an office. The boundary between work and private life can also become blurred, leading some employees to work longer hours than before and to struggle to switch off. From a company's perspective, collaboration and the training of new staff can be more difficult when colleagues rarely meet face to face, and junior employees may lose the opportunity to learn by observing experienced colleagues.

However, most of these problems can be reduced through sensible management. A hybrid model, in which staff spend two or three days in the office and the remainder at home, allows teams to maintain personal relationships while still enjoying flexibility. Clear rules about working hours can also help people to protect their free time.

In conclusion, while remote working presents certain challenges, its benefits in terms of time, cost and flexibility outweigh them, especially when it is organised thoughtfully.

question:
Write about the following topic:

In many countries, more and more people are moving from rural areas to cities.

Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Across much of the world, the population of towns and cities is growing rapidly as people leave the countryside. In this essay, I will explain the main reasons for this movement and argue that, although it brings some problems, it is largely a positive development.

The primary reason for urban migration is economic. Cities offer a far wider range of jobs, and wages are usually higher than in rural areas, where employment often depends on agriculture, a sector that has become increasingly mechanised and therefore requires fewer workers. In addition, cities provide better access to services such as hospitals, universities and specialist shops. Young people in particular are attracted by the educational opportunities and the lively social and cultural life that urban areas offer.

In many respects, this trend is beneficial. When people move to cities, they generally gain access to better-paid work, which raises living standards and allows them to support family members who remain in the countryside. Cities are also centres of innovation, because they bring together large numbers of skilled people and businesses. Moreover, providing infrastructure such as public transport, clean water and broadband is more efficient in densely populated areas.

Nevertheless, rapid urbanisation can create serious difficulties. If cities grow faster than housing and transport can be provided, the result may be overcrowding, rising rents and traffic congestion. Meanwhile, rural communities may decline as young people leave, leaving an ageing population and closing schools and shops.

In conclusion, people move to cities mainly for better jobs and services. Provided that governments plan urban growth carefully and continue to support rural areas, I believe this movement is, on balance, a positive development.

passage: Essay type: Opinion (To what extent do you agree or disagree?)
question:
Write about the following topic:

Governments should spend money on improving public transport rather than building new roads.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Transport infrastructure absorbs a substantial proportion of public spending in most countries, and there is ongoing debate about how this money should be allocated. I largely agree that public transport deserves priority over road construction, although new roads remain necessary in certain circumstances.

The strongest argument for investing in public transport is that it moves people far more efficiently than private cars. A single train can carry over a thousand passengers, occupying a fraction of the space that the equivalent number of cars would require. Building more roads, by contrast, often fails to reduce congestion in the long term, because improved roads encourage more people to drive, a phenomenon known as induced demand. In addition, public transport produces considerably lower emissions per passenger, so investment in it supports national commitments to reduce air pollution and tackle climate change.

There are also important social benefits. Not everyone can afford to own a car or is able to drive, including many elderly people, students and those on low incomes. Affordable buses and trains give these groups access to employment, education and healthcare, thereby reducing inequality. Well-designed transport networks can also revitalise city centres by bringing in visitors without the need for large car parks.

Nonetheless, it would be unrealistic to stop building roads altogether. In rural and remote regions, populations are too scattered for public transport to be economically viable, and decent roads are essential for residents and for the delivery of goods. Furthermore, buses themselves depend on a well-maintained road network.

In conclusion, while roads will always have a role to play, governments should direct the majority of transport funding towards public transport, which offers greater environmental, economic and social returns.

passage: Essay type: Discuss both views and give your opinion
question:
Write about the following topic:

Some people think that keeping animals in zoos is cruel and should be stopped. Others believe that zoos play an important role in protecting wildlife.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Zoos have existed for centuries, but their role in modern society is increasingly controversial. While some people consider them cruel, others maintain that they make a valuable contribution to conservation. I believe that well-run zoos can be justified, but only if they meet strict standards of animal welfare.

Those who oppose zoos argue that it is morally wrong to confine wild animals for human entertainment. Even in large enclosures, animals such as elephants or big cats have far less space than they would in the wild, and some display signs of stress, such as pacing repeatedly or harming themselves. Critics also point out that many zoos are primarily commercial businesses whose main concern is attracting paying visitors rather than protecting animals.

On the other hand, supporters claim that modern zoos are essential for protecting endangered species. Breeding programmes in zoos have helped to save several animals from extinction and, in some cases, to reintroduce them into their natural habitats. Zoos also fund field research and conservation projects around the world. Furthermore, they have an educational role: seeing animals in person can inspire children to care about wildlife and the environment in a way that books or videos may not.

In my opinion, both arguments have merit, which is why the quality of a zoo is the crucial factor. Zoos that provide spacious, natural environments, focus on endangered species and take part in genuine conservation work deserve support. However, small, poorly managed zoos that keep animals mainly for display should be closed.

In conclusion, zoos are neither entirely good nor entirely bad. With strict regulation, they can protect wildlife while respecting the welfare of the animals in their care.

question:
Write about the following topic:

In many countries, an increasing number of people are choosing to live alone.

Why is this? Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
In a growing number of countries, single-person households have become one of the most common types of household. This essay will consider the reasons behind this trend and argue that it has both positive and negative aspects, although its overall impact depends largely on whether people live alone by choice.

Several factors explain this development. Firstly, economic independence has increased, particularly among women, so more people can afford their own accommodation without relying on a partner or family. Secondly, attitudes towards marriage have changed: people are marrying later, and divorce has become more socially acceptable, meaning that many adults spend long periods of their lives without a partner. Finally, in ageing societies, a large number of elderly people live alone after the death of a spouse.

For many, living alone is a positive experience. It offers privacy, freedom and the opportunity to organise one's life according to personal preferences. Young professionals, for example, may value the chance to focus on their careers and develop a strong sense of independence. In this respect, the trend reflects greater individual freedom and choice.

However, there are also significant drawbacks. Single-person households consume more resources per person, such as housing, energy and household goods, which places pressure on the housing market and the environment. More seriously, living alone can lead to loneliness and social isolation, particularly among older people, which research has linked to poorer physical and mental health.

In conclusion, the rise in solo living stems from economic independence, changing social attitudes and population ageing. While it can be a liberating choice, governments and communities should ensure that people who live alone, especially the elderly, remain socially connected.

passage: Essay type: Opinion (To what extent do you agree or disagree?)
question:
Write about the following topic:

Social media has a more negative than positive effect on young people.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Social media platforms have become a central part of most teenagers' lives. While they offer genuine benefits, I agree to a large extent that their negative effects on young people currently outweigh the positive ones.

It must be acknowledged that social media has some advantages. It enables young people to stay in touch with friends and family, including those who live far away. It can also provide valuable support for teenagers who feel isolated, for example those with unusual interests or health conditions, who can find communities of like-minded people online. Moreover, many young people use these platforms creatively, sharing music, art or videos and even developing skills that may help them in their future careers.

Nevertheless, the drawbacks are serious. The most widely discussed is the impact on mental health. Platforms constantly present carefully edited images of other people's lives and appearances, which can lead young users to compare themselves unfavourably and suffer from low self-esteem or anxiety. Cyberbullying is another major concern, since hurtful comments can reach a victim at any time of day and be seen by a large audience. In addition, social media applications are deliberately designed to keep users scrolling, and excessive use can reduce the time young people spend sleeping, studying and taking part in physical activity.

These problems are particularly worrying because adolescents are still developing emotionally and may find it harder than adults to manage their online habits. Therefore, while social media is not inherently harmful, its current design tends to exploit the vulnerabilities of young users.

In conclusion, although social media can connect and inspire young people, its negative effects on their wellbeing are, in my view, more significant, and stronger regulation and education are needed.

What are the causes of this problem? What can be done to solve it?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Childhood obesity has become a significant public health concern in many parts of the world. Overweight children are more likely to develop serious illnesses later in life, so it is important to understand why this is happening and how it can be addressed.

One major cause is diet. Highly processed foods and sugary drinks are cheap, widely available and heavily advertised to children, and many families rely on them because they are convenient. Busy parents may have little time to cook healthy meals, and some may lack knowledge about nutrition. A second cause is a decline in physical activity. Children today spend far more time on screens, whether watching videos or playing computer games, and less time playing outdoors. In many cities, concerns about traffic and safety mean that children are driven to school rather than walking or cycling.

To tackle this problem, action is needed at several levels. Governments could restrict the advertising of unhealthy food during children's television programmes and online, and introduce taxes on sugary drinks, which have led to reduced consumption in some countries. Schools also have a vital role. They can provide nutritious lunches, teach basic cooking skills and ensure that pupils have at least one hour of physical activity every day. Finally, parents should be encouraged to set limits on screen time and to make exercise a regular family activity, for example by walking or cycling together at weekends.

In conclusion, the rise in childhood obesity is mainly caused by unhealthy diets and inactive lifestyles. Only a combination of government regulation, school programmes and parental involvement is likely to reverse this worrying trend.

question:
Write about the following topic:

Some people believe that international tourism brings enormous benefits to countries. Others think that the number of tourists should be limited because of the problems they cause.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
International tourism has expanded dramatically in recent decades, bringing millions of visitors to destinations around the world. While some regard this as an unquestionable benefit, others argue that tourist numbers should be restricted. In my view, tourism is valuable, but popular destinations need to manage visitor numbers carefully.

Those who welcome tourism emphasise its economic contribution. In many countries, it is a major source of income and employment, supporting not only hotels and restaurants but also transport companies, local craftspeople and farmers. Tourism can also fund the preservation of historic buildings and natural areas, since governments have a financial incentive to maintain attractions that draw visitors. In addition, travel promotes cultural exchange, allowing people to understand ways of life different from their own.

However, critics point to the problems caused by mass tourism. In some famous cities, the number of visitors far exceeds the local population at peak times, causing overcrowding and placing pressure on public services. The growth of short-term holiday rentals has also pushed up housing costs, forcing some residents out of their own neighbourhoods. Environmental damage is another concern, as fragile ecosystems such as coral reefs and mountain trails can be harmed by large numbers of visitors, and air travel contributes significantly to carbon emissions.

I believe the solution lies in managing tourism rather than simply limiting or promoting it. Measures such as daily visitor caps at vulnerable sites, tourist taxes that fund local services, and campaigns encouraging travel to less-visited regions can preserve the benefits of tourism while reducing its harm.

In conclusion, international tourism brings considerable economic and cultural advantages, but these can only be sustained if destinations take active steps to control its negative effects.

question:
Write about the following topic:

More and more people are choosing to shop online rather than in traditional shops.

What are the advantages and disadvantages of this trend?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
The rise of online shopping has transformed the way people buy everything from groceries to furniture. This essay will discuss the main advantages and disadvantages of this trend for consumers and for society.

For consumers, the greatest advantage of online shopping is convenience. People can buy products at any time of day without leaving their homes, which is especially helpful for those with busy schedules, young children or limited mobility. Online shops also offer a far wider range of goods than most physical stores, and customers can easily compare prices and read reviews before making a decision, which often enables them to find better deals. In addition, home delivery saves the time and cost of travelling to shops.

However, there are also several disadvantages. Firstly, customers cannot see, touch or try on products before buying them, so items sometimes turn out to be different from their descriptions, and returning them can be inconvenient. Secondly, the growth of online retail has had a damaging effect on traditional high streets. Many local shops have been forced to close, leading to job losses and leaving town centres empty and less attractive. Thirdly, the large number of individual deliveries increases traffic and packaging waste, which has negative consequences for the environment. Finally, online shopping reduces the social interaction that people used to enjoy when visiting local markets and shops.

In conclusion, online shopping offers clear benefits in terms of convenience, choice and price. Nevertheless, its effects on local communities and the environment are significant, so it is important that people continue to support local businesses and that retailers reduce unnecessary packaging.

passage: Essay type: Opinion (To what extent do you agree or disagree?)
question:
Write about the following topic:

Some people believe that all secondary school students should be required to do unpaid work in their local community as part of their education.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
There is a growing view that teenagers should be obliged to carry out voluntary work, such as helping in care homes or cleaning public spaces, as part of their schooling. I largely agree with this idea, provided that the work is meaningful and does not interfere with students' academic studies.

The main benefit of compulsory community service is that it helps young people develop a sense of social responsibility. Many teenagers have little contact with people outside their own age group or social background. Working alongside elderly residents, people with disabilities or local charities can broaden their understanding of society and encourage empathy. Such experiences may also inspire some students to continue volunteering as adults, which strengthens communities in the long term.

In addition, community work allows students to develop practical skills that are rarely taught in the classroom. Organising a charity event or helping at a food bank requires teamwork, communication and problem-solving, all of which are highly valued by employers and universities. It can also help students to discover interests that influence their future career choices, for example in healthcare, education or environmental protection.

Admittedly, there are some valid concerns. Secondary students already face heavy workloads and pressure to perform well in examinations, and additional obligations could cause stress. Furthermore, some critics argue that work which is compulsory is no longer truly voluntary, and students who are forced to participate may not take it seriously. These problems, however, could be minimised if schools limited the requirement to a reasonable number of hours per year and allowed students to choose the type of activity they find most worthwhile.

In conclusion, I believe that a well-designed programme of community service would benefit both students and society.

passage: Essay type: Two-part question
question:
Write about the following topic:

Nowadays, many people, especially young people, rarely read books for pleasure.

Why is this the case? What could be done to encourage people to read more?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Although books are more accessible than ever, it appears that fewer people, particularly the young, choose to read for enjoyment. This essay will examine the reasons for this decline and suggest some ways of encouraging reading.

The most obvious reason is the competition from digital entertainment. Smartphones, video streaming services and online games offer instant, highly stimulating entertainment that requires little effort, whereas reading a novel demands sustained concentration. As people become used to short videos and constant notifications, many find it difficult to focus on a long text. Another reason is lack of time. Students often have heavy workloads, and adults with demanding jobs may feel too tired in the evening to read. Furthermore, if reading is associated mainly with schoolwork and examinations, young people may come to regard it as a duty rather than a pleasure.

Several measures could help to reverse this trend. At school, teachers could allow students to choose books that genuinely interest them, including graphic novels or science fiction, rather than relying solely on classic texts. Setting aside a short period each day for silent reading has also proved successful in many schools. Parents play an important role too: children who see their parents reading and who are read to at a young age are much more likely to become lifelong readers. Finally, libraries and publishers could make use of technology rather than competing with it, for example by offering free e-books and audiobooks, or by organising online book clubs where young readers can share their opinions.

In conclusion, the decline in reading is largely caused by digital distractions and busy lifestyles, but schools, families and libraries can work together to make reading an enjoyable habit once again.

passage: Essay type: Discuss both views and give your opinion
question:
Write about the following topic:

Some people think that governments should spend money on exploring outer space. Others believe this money should be used to solve problems on Earth.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Space exploration is one of the most ambitious and expensive activities undertaken by governments. Some people regard it as a worthwhile investment, while others believe the money would be better spent addressing urgent problems on our own planet. In my view, although pressing earthly issues must take priority, a modest level of space funding is justified.

Those who oppose space programmes argue that it is difficult to justify spending billions on rockets and probes while millions of people lack access to clean water, healthcare or education. They also point out that problems such as climate change and poverty require immediate action, whereas the benefits of space exploration are uncertain and long-term. From this perspective, every pound spent on sending equipment to Mars is a pound that could have been used to improve people's lives today.

Supporters, however, maintain that space research has delivered enormous practical benefits. Satellites, originally developed as part of space programmes, are now essential for weather forecasting, navigation and communication, and they play a crucial role in monitoring deforestation and climate change. Many technologies used in medicine and everyday products also originated in space research. Furthermore, exploration inspires young people to study science and engineering, which strengthens a country's capacity for innovation.

I believe that the two goals are not necessarily in conflict. Space budgets typically represent only a small fraction of total government spending, and much of the knowledge they generate directly helps us to understand and protect the Earth. Nevertheless, governments should ensure that such projects are transparent and focused on research with clear scientific or social value.

In conclusion, while solving problems on Earth must remain the highest priority, a balanced investment in space exploration can contribute to that very aim.

passage: Essay type: Problem and solution
question:
Write about the following topic:

In many countries, large amounts of food are thrown away every day by households, supermarkets and restaurants.

Why does this happen? What can be done to reduce food waste?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Despite the fact that millions of people around the world do not have enough to eat, a huge quantity of food is wasted every day in wealthier societies. This essay will discuss the main causes of food waste and suggest some measures to reduce it.

At the household level, much food is wasted because of poor planning. People often buy more than they need, particularly when supermarkets offer special deals such as "buy one, get one free". As a result, fresh products such as fruit, vegetables and bread go off before they can be eaten. Confusion over date labels is another factor: many consumers throw away food that has passed its "best before" date, even though it is still perfectly safe to eat. In the retail sector, supermarkets reject produce that does not meet strict standards of appearance, while restaurants frequently serve portions that are too large for customers to finish.

A number of steps could be taken to address this problem. Firstly, governments could run public awareness campaigns explaining the difference between "use by" and "best before" dates and encouraging people to plan their meals and shopping more carefully. Secondly, supermarkets could be required by law to donate unsold but edible food to charities instead of throwing it away, as has happened in some countries. They could also sell imperfect fruit and vegetables at lower prices rather than rejecting them. Thirdly, restaurants could offer smaller portion sizes and make it easy for customers to take leftover food home.

In conclusion, food waste results from consumer habits, confusing labels and commercial practices. A combination of education, regulation and changes in business behaviour could significantly reduce the amount of food that ends up in the bin.

passage: Essay type: Opinion (To what extent do you agree or disagree?)
question:
Write about the following topic:

Some people believe that in the future, computers and artificial intelligence will completely replace teachers in the classroom.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Advances in artificial intelligence have led some commentators to predict that human teachers will soon become unnecessary. While I accept that technology will play an increasingly important role in education, I strongly disagree that it will ever completely replace teachers.

It is true that AI-based learning tools have impressive capabilities. Adaptive software can assess a student's level instantly and provide exercises tailored to their individual needs, something a teacher with thirty pupils cannot always do. Such programmes are available at any time, never lose patience and can give immediate feedback on tasks such as grammar exercises or mathematics problems. In regions where qualified teachers are scarce, these tools could make high-quality instruction available to far more learners.

However, education involves far more than the transmission of information. One of a teacher's most important roles is to motivate students, particularly those who lack confidence or who have difficulties at home. A good teacher notices when a child is upset or disengaged and responds with encouragement, something that depends on genuine human relationships. Schools are also where young people learn social skills, such as cooperation, conflict resolution and respect for others, and these are best developed under the guidance of an adult who can model appropriate behaviour.

Furthermore, critical thinking and creativity are often developed through discussion, debate and open-ended projects, in which teachers ask probing questions and challenge students' assumptions. Although AI may be able to imitate parts of this process, it cannot take responsibility for children's wellbeing or exercise moral judgement in complex situations.

In conclusion, AI will undoubtedly transform the way students learn, but it is likely to serve as a powerful assistant to teachers rather than a substitute for them.

question:
Write about the following topic:

An increasing number of students choose to go abroad to study at university.

Do the advantages of studying abroad outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Every year, millions of young people leave their home countries to study at foreign universities. Although studying abroad has some disadvantages, I believe that its advantages are considerably greater.

The most obvious benefit is academic. Students may gain access to world-class universities, specialist courses or research facilities that are not available in their own country. Studying in a different educational system can also introduce them to new teaching styles and ways of thinking. In addition, living abroad usually means studying in a foreign language, so students can achieve a level of fluency that would be difficult to reach at home.

There are also important personal benefits. Living independently in an unfamiliar environment forces young people to manage their own finances, solve practical problems and adapt to different customs. This experience often makes them more confident and mature. Furthermore, international students build friendships and professional networks with people from many countries, which can be extremely valuable in today's globalised job market, where employers seek graduates with intercultural skills.

On the other hand, studying abroad has some drawbacks. The cost of tuition fees, accommodation and travel can be very high, and not all families can afford it. Many students also suffer from homesickness and culture shock, especially during their first few months, and language difficulties can make lectures and assignments more challenging. In some cases, qualifications obtained overseas may not be fully recognised by employers at home.

However, most of these difficulties are temporary or can be reduced through scholarships and university support services. In conclusion, while studying abroad can be expensive and emotionally demanding, the academic, linguistic and personal benefits it offers make it a highly worthwhile experience.

question:
Write about the following topic:

Some people think that there should be a fixed age at which all workers must retire.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
In many countries, there has traditionally been an official retirement age, after which people are expected to stop working. Some people believe this rule should apply to everyone. I disagree with this view, as I think the decision to retire should depend on individual circumstances.

Those who support a fixed retirement age argue that it creates opportunities for younger people. When older employees retire, positions become available for the next generation, which may help to reduce youth unemployment. Supporters also claim that a clear rule is fair and simple, because it treats everyone equally and allows companies to plan their workforce in advance. In physically demanding jobs, such as construction, a set retirement age may also protect older workers from injury.

However, I believe these arguments are outweighed by the disadvantages. Firstly, people age very differently. Many people in their sixties and seventies are healthy, energetic and highly productive, and forcing them to stop working wastes their skills and experience. Secondly, in an era of rising life expectancy, many people need to keep earning in order to support themselves for longer, especially if their pension savings are insufficient. Thirdly, work provides older people with a sense of purpose and social contact, both of which are important for mental and physical health.

Moreover, the claim that older workers take jobs from younger people is questionable, since the number of jobs in an economy is not fixed. Experienced employees can also mentor younger colleagues, benefiting the whole organisation.

In conclusion, rather than imposing a single retirement age on everyone, governments should allow people to choose when to retire, while ensuring that those in physically demanding jobs can retire earlier if necessary.

question:
Write about the following topic:

Fast food is becoming more and more popular around the world.

Why is this happening? Should governments discourage people from eating fast food, for example by taxing it?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Fast food restaurants can now be found in almost every town and city in the world, and their popularity continues to grow. This essay will explore why this is happening and argue that governments should take some action to discourage excessive consumption, although taxation alone is not enough.

There are several reasons for the popularity of fast food. The most important is convenience. In modern societies, many people work long hours and have little time or energy to cook, so a meal that is ready in minutes is very attractive. Fast food is also relatively cheap, which appeals to students and families on tight budgets. In addition, large fast-food companies spend huge sums on advertising, often targeting children, and their products are designed to taste good, being high in salt, sugar and fat.

Because regular consumption of such food contributes to obesity, heart disease and diabetes, I believe governments have a responsibility to intervene. A tax on unhealthy food or sugary drinks could reduce consumption and raise money for public health programmes, and such taxes have had some success in several countries. However, taxes can be unfair to people on low incomes, who may have fewer alternatives. For this reason, they should be combined with other measures. For example, governments could make healthy food more affordable, require restaurants to display calorie information clearly, and restrict fast-food advertising aimed at children. Education about nutrition and cooking in schools would also help young people to make healthier choices.

In conclusion, fast food is popular because it is convenient, cheap and heavily marketed. Governments should discourage excessive consumption, but through a combination of taxation, regulation and education rather than tax alone.

question:
Write about the following topic:

Many of the world's languages are spoken by only a small number of people, and some are in danger of disappearing completely.

Why is this happening? What can be done to protect these languages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Linguists estimate that a significant proportion of the world's languages may disappear by the end of this century. This essay will examine why so many languages are endangered and propose some measures to protect them.

The decline of minority languages is closely linked to globalisation and economic change. In order to find work, access higher education or move to cities, people increasingly need to speak a dominant national or international language. Parents may therefore decide that it is more useful for their children to speak the majority language at home, and within one or two generations, the minority language is no longer passed on. The media also plays a part: television, the internet and popular music are overwhelmingly produced in a small number of major languages, which makes them seem more modern and prestigious. In some cases, past government policies discouraged or even banned the use of minority languages in schools.

Protecting endangered languages requires action on several fronts. Firstly, education is crucial. Bilingual schools, in which children are taught in both the minority and the majority language, have helped to revive languages in a number of regions. Secondly, governments can give minority languages official status, so that they are used on road signs, in public services and in local media, thereby increasing their visibility and prestige. Thirdly, technology can be used positively: recording elderly speakers, creating online dictionaries and developing language-learning apps can help to preserve and teach languages that have few remaining speakers.

In conclusion, languages are disappearing mainly because of economic pressures and the dominance of major languages. With supportive education policies, official recognition and the creative use of technology, however, many of them can still be saved.

question:
Write about the following topic:

Some people believe that schools should teach children how to manage money. Others think this is the responsibility of parents.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Financial skills, such as budgeting and saving, are essential in adult life, yet many young people leave school without them. While some argue that schools should teach these skills, others believe that parents are better placed to do so. In my view, both have an important role, but schools should take the lead.

Those who think parents should be responsible argue that money is a practical, everyday matter best learned at home. Children can observe how their parents plan a weekly shopping budget, pay bills and save for holidays. Giving children pocket money and allowing them to make their own spending decisions can also teach them valuable lessons. Moreover, attitudes towards money are often personal and linked to family values, so some people feel that parents should guide their children in this area.

On the other hand, supporters of financial education in schools point out that not all parents have the knowledge or confidence to teach these skills. Some adults themselves struggle with debt or do not understand concepts such as interest rates, loans and taxes. If financial education is left entirely to families, children from less advantaged backgrounds may be at a disadvantage. Schools, by contrast, can provide every child with accurate, up-to-date information, and they can teach it systematically through practical activities, such as planning a monthly budget or comparing mobile phone contracts.

I believe that schools should provide a basic financial education to ensure that all children have the same opportunities, while parents should reinforce these lessons at home through everyday examples.

In conclusion, although parents have a valuable role to play, schools are in a better position to guarantee that every young person develops the financial skills needed in adult life.

passage: Essay type: Positive or negative development
question:
Write about the following topic:

In many countries, people are using cash less and less, and paying for most things by card or mobile phone.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
In many parts of the world, coins and banknotes are rapidly being replaced by contactless cards and mobile payment apps. Although this shift towards a cashless society offers clear benefits, I believe it also carries risks that must be carefully managed.

There are several advantages to digital payments. The most obvious is convenience: paying with a card or phone is quick, and consumers no longer need to visit cash machines or carry heavy coins. For businesses, digital payments reduce the time spent counting and transporting cash and lower the risk of theft. Electronic transactions also leave a record, which makes it more difficult to evade taxes or carry out illegal activities such as money laundering. In addition, many people find it easier to track their spending through banking apps, helping them to manage their budgets.

However, a society without cash could create significant problems. Firstly, it may exclude vulnerable groups, including many elderly people, those without bank accounts and people who are not confident using technology. If shops and public services stop accepting cash, these individuals could find it difficult to buy basic necessities. Secondly, digital systems depend on electricity and internet connections, so technical failures or cyber-attacks could temporarily prevent people from paying for anything at all. Thirdly, there are concerns about privacy, as every electronic purchase generates data that can be collected and analysed by banks and technology companies.

On balance, I consider the move away from cash to be a largely positive development, because of its convenience and security. Nevertheless, governments should ensure that cash remains widely accepted for those who need it, and that strong regulations protect consumers' data.

In conclusion, a cashless society brings efficiency and transparency, but it must not leave anyone behind.

question:
Write about the following topic:

Professional athletes and entertainers earn far more money than people in essential jobs such as nurses and teachers. This is unfair.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
It is often pointed out that a top footballer may earn more in a week than a nurse earns in several years. While I understand why such salaries exist, I agree that this situation is unfair, since it does not reflect the true value of different jobs to society.

There are reasons why sports stars and entertainers receive such high incomes. Their salaries are determined by the market: a famous athlete or singer can attract millions of fans, generating enormous revenue from tickets, broadcasting rights and advertising. In addition, their careers are often short and highly uncertain. Only a tiny proportion of people who train for years ever reach the top, and many athletes must retire in their thirties. From this perspective, high pay can be seen as a reward for exceptional talent and dedication.

However, I believe these arguments do not justify the enormous gap in earnings. Nurses, teachers and other essential workers make a far greater contribution to society. Nurses care for people when they are most vulnerable, and teachers shape the knowledge and character of future generations. Their work requires years of training, involves considerable stress and responsibility, and continues throughout a long career. Yet many of these professionals struggle with rising living costs, and some countries face shortages of nurses and teachers partly because the pay is not attractive enough.

Of course, it would be unrealistic to set a legal limit on what entertainers can earn. Instead, governments should ensure that essential workers are paid fairly and should consider higher taxes on very large incomes, using the revenue to fund public services.

In conclusion, although celebrity salaries are a product of market forces, the gap between them and the pay of essential workers is unfair and should be reduced.

question:
Write about the following topic:

Many people today suffer from stress caused by their work.

What are the causes of work-related stress? What can be done to reduce it?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Work-related stress has become a widespread problem in many modern workplaces, leading to health problems, absence from work and reduced productivity. This essay will discuss the main causes of this stress and suggest some possible solutions.

One of the main causes of stress at work is excessive workload. As companies try to reduce costs, many employees are expected to do the work of more than one person, often within tight deadlines. Long working hours leave little time for rest, exercise or family life. A second cause is technology. Smartphones and email mean that employees can be contacted at any time, and many feel under pressure to reply to messages in the evenings and at weekends, so they never fully switch off. Job insecurity is another important factor, since fears about redundancy can create constant anxiety. Finally, poor relationships with managers or colleagues, including a lack of recognition or support, can make the working environment unpleasant.

There are several ways to reduce work-related stress. Employers have the greatest responsibility. They should ensure that workloads are realistic and that staff are not expected to work excessive overtime. Some companies have introduced policies that restrict emails outside working hours, which helps employees to rest properly. Managers can also be trained to recognise signs of stress and to communicate openly and supportively with their teams. Offering flexible working arrangements and access to counselling services can also make a significant difference.

At the same time, individuals can take steps to protect their own wellbeing, such as taking regular breaks, exercising and learning to set boundaries.

In conclusion, work-related stress is caused mainly by heavy workloads, constant connectivity and insecurity, but it can be reduced through better management practices and healthy personal habits.

question:
Write about the following topic:

Some people think that studying history is a waste of time, as students should focus on subjects that prepare them for the future. Others believe history is an essential subject.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
With the rapid growth of technology, some people question whether school time should be devoted to studying the past. While there are understandable reasons for this view, I firmly believe that history remains an essential part of education.

Those who consider history less important argue that the modern world demands practical, forward-looking skills. Subjects such as computer science, mathematics and engineering prepare students directly for well-paid jobs in growing industries, and the school timetable is limited. From this perspective, memorising the dates of ancient battles or the names of past rulers seems to have little relevance to young people who will work in a digital economy. They also suggest that anyone interested in history can easily learn about it independently through books, documentaries or the internet.

However, this view misunderstands what history teaches. Studying history is not simply about memorising facts; it involves analysing sources, comparing different interpretations and constructing evidence-based arguments. These analytical skills are highly transferable and are valuable in professions as diverse as law, journalism and business. More importantly, history helps students to understand how the present world came to be. Current political conflicts, economic systems and social movements cannot be properly understood without knowledge of their origins.

History also has a civic role. By learning about past injustices, wars and the struggles for rights and freedoms, young people can develop empathy and become informed citizens who are less likely to be misled by propaganda or simplistic explanations. In an age of widespread misinformation, the ability to evaluate sources critically is arguably more important than ever.

In conclusion, although future-oriented subjects are clearly important, history equips students with critical skills and understanding that are equally vital, and it should remain a core subject.

passage: Essay type: Opinion (To what extent do you agree or disagree?)
question:
Write about the following topic:

Governments should ban the use of plastic packaging for food and other products.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Plastic packaging is used for almost every product we buy, from fruit and vegetables to electronic goods. Because of its impact on the environment, some people believe it should be banned. I partly agree with this view: unnecessary plastic packaging should be prohibited, but a complete ban would not be practical at present.

There are strong environmental arguments for restricting plastic packaging. Most plastic is used only once before being thrown away, and a large proportion is never recycled. Instead, it ends up in landfill sites, where it can take hundreds of years to break down, or in rivers and oceans, where it harms marine animals that become trapped in it or swallow it. Tiny fragments known as microplastics have now been found in drinking water and even in the human body. Banning plastic packaging would force manufacturers to develop alternatives, such as paper, glass or biodegradable materials.

However, plastic packaging also has important benefits. In the food industry, it keeps products fresh for longer, which reduces food waste, an environmental problem in its own right. It is also light, which means that transporting goods requires less fuel than if heavier materials such as glass were used. In medicine, sterile plastic packaging is essential for hygiene and safety. Replacing all plastic immediately could therefore increase costs and create new environmental problems.

For these reasons, I believe a more effective approach would be to ban single-use plastics that are clearly unnecessary, such as plastic bags, straws and excessive wrapping on fruit, while taxing other plastic packaging and investing in recycling and alternative materials.

In conclusion, although a total ban is unrealistic, governments should take firm action to reduce plastic packaging wherever suitable alternatives exist.

passage: Essay type: Two-part question
question:
Write about the following topic:

In many countries, young adults are living with their parents for much longer than in the past.

Why is this happening? Do the advantages of this situation outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
In many parts of the world, it has become increasingly common for people in their twenties and even thirties to continue living in the family home. This essay will examine the reasons for this trend and argue that, while it has certain benefits, its disadvantages are more significant in the long term.

The primary reason is economic. In many cities, housing costs have risen much faster than wages, making it extremely difficult for young people to afford rent, let alone save for a deposit to buy a home. At the same time, more young adults are spending longer in higher education, often accumulating student debt, and starting salaries in many sectors remain low. Job insecurity, including short-term contracts, also makes young people reluctant to commit to long-term rental agreements. Cultural factors play a part as well: in some societies, living with parents until marriage is considered normal and desirable.

This arrangement certainly has advantages. Young adults can save money, pay off debts and build financial security before moving out. Families may also benefit from closer relationships, and adult children can provide practical support to ageing parents.

However, the disadvantages are considerable. Living with parents for too long may delay the development of independence and important life skills, such as managing a household budget. It can also cause tension within families, as adult children and parents may have different expectations about privacy and responsibilities. On a broader level, delays in leaving home are associated with later marriage and lower birth rates, which may contribute to population ageing.

In conclusion, young adults stay at home longer mainly because of financial pressures. Although this offers short-term benefits, it can limit independence, so governments should address the underlying problem of housing affordability.

passage: Essay type: Discuss both views and give your opinion
question:
Write about the following topic:

Some people believe that the best way to reduce crime is to give longer prison sentences. Others think there are better alternatives.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Crime prevention is a central concern for every government, but there is considerable disagreement about the most effective approach. While some advocate longer prison sentences, others argue that alternative strategies are more successful. In my opinion, although prison is necessary for serious offenders, longer sentences alone are not the most effective way to reduce crime.

Supporters of longer sentences put forward two main arguments. Firstly, they believe that harsh punishment acts as a deterrent: if potential criminals know they face many years in prison, they will be less likely to break the law. Secondly, keeping dangerous offenders in prison for longer protects the public, because they are unable to commit further crimes while they are locked up. Many victims of crime also feel that long sentences deliver justice.

However, there is considerable evidence that the threat of long sentences has a limited deterrent effect, as many crimes are committed impulsively or by people who do not expect to be caught. Moreover, prisons can become schools of crime, where offenders, particularly young ones, form connections with more experienced criminals. On release, former prisoners often struggle to find work or housing, and many reoffend. Long sentences are also extremely expensive for taxpayers.

Alternative approaches focus on addressing the causes of crime. Education and vocational training in prison, drug treatment programmes and community sentences for minor offences have been shown to reduce reoffending in a number of countries. Investing in early intervention, such as youth programmes in disadvantaged areas, can also prevent young people from turning to crime in the first place.

In conclusion, while prison remains essential for protecting the public from dangerous criminals, crime is more effectively reduced through rehabilitation and prevention than through longer sentences.

question:
Write about the following topic:

All children should be taught how to cook at school.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Cooking is a basic life skill, but many young people today leave home without knowing how to prepare a simple meal. I strongly agree that cooking should be taught to all children at school, as it brings benefits for their health, their independence and even their academic learning.

The most important reason is health. Many families rely heavily on ready meals and takeaway food, which are often high in salt, sugar and fat. If children learn how to cook fresh, balanced meals at school, they will be more likely to eat healthily as adults. Cooking lessons can also teach children about nutrition, such as the importance of vegetables and the dangers of too much sugar, in a practical way that they are likely to remember.

Secondly, cooking helps young people to become independent. When students go to university or start living alone, they need to feed themselves on a limited budget. Knowing how to plan meals, shop wisely and use leftovers can save them a great deal of money and reduce food waste.

Thirdly, cooking lessons can support other subjects. Measuring ingredients and adjusting recipes involve mathematics, while learning about where food comes from can be linked to science and geography. Working together in the kitchen also develops teamwork and communication skills.

Some people argue that schools do not have enough time or money to offer cooking lessons, and that this is the responsibility of parents. However, not all parents have the time or skills to teach their children, and school lessons ensure that every child has the same opportunity.

In conclusion, I believe that cooking lessons are a valuable investment in children's health and future, and they should be part of every school curriculum.

passage: Essay type: Positive or negative development
question:
Write about the following topic:

More and more people now get their news from social media rather than from newspapers or television.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
In recent years, social media platforms have become the main source of news for a growing number of people, particularly the young. While this trend has made information more accessible, I believe its overall effect is negative, mainly because of its impact on the quality and reliability of the news people receive.

There are undeniable benefits to this development. Social media allows news to spread almost instantly, so people can learn about important events, such as natural disasters, as they happen. It also gives a voice to ordinary citizens, who can share eyewitness reports and highlight issues that traditional media might ignore. In addition, news on social media is usually free and easy to access on a smartphone, which may encourage people who would never buy a newspaper to follow current affairs.

However, the drawbacks are serious. Unlike professional journalists, many people who share news online do not check facts, so false or misleading stories can spread rapidly and reach millions of users before they are corrected. Furthermore, social media platforms use algorithms that show users content similar to what they have previously liked. As a result, people are often exposed mainly to views that confirm their existing opinions, which can increase political polarisation. News on social media also tends to be presented in short, emotional formats, which may discourage people from engaging with complex issues in depth.

Another concern is the economic impact on traditional journalism. As advertising revenue shifts to online platforms, many newspapers have reduced their staff or closed, weakening investigative reporting, which plays a vital role in holding governments and businesses accountable.

In conclusion, although social media makes news faster and more accessible, its tendency to spread misinformation and narrow people's perspectives makes this development largely negative.

passage: Essay type: Problem and solution
question:
Write about the following topic:

In many countries, the populations of small villages and rural areas are declining as people move away.

What problems does this cause? What can be done to solve these problems?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
In many countries, rural communities are shrinking as residents, especially young people, leave for towns and cities. This trend creates a number of serious problems, but there are also measures that could help to address them.

The most immediate problem is the decline of local services. When the population falls, there are fewer customers for shops, post offices and banks, so many of them close. Schools may also shut down because there are not enough pupils, forcing remaining families to travel long distances. Public transport becomes less frequent, making life particularly difficult for elderly residents who do not drive. A second problem is the ageing of rural populations. Since it is mainly young people who leave, villages are increasingly left with older residents who may need healthcare and support but have fewer younger people nearby to help them. Finally, the loss of population can lead to abandoned houses and farmland, and local traditions and community life may gradually disappear.

Several solutions could be considered. Firstly, governments should invest in fast and reliable internet connections in rural areas. This would allow people to work remotely, run online businesses and access services such as telemedicine, making it possible to live in the countryside without sacrificing career opportunities. Secondly, financial incentives, such as grants for young families who move to rural areas or low-cost housing schemes, could attract new residents. Thirdly, local services could be combined, for example by creating community centres that include a shop, a post office and a clinic in the same building, making them more economically sustainable.

In conclusion, rural depopulation threatens local services and community life, but improved digital infrastructure, incentives for new residents and creative approaches to services could help to revitalise these areas.

passage: Essay type: Discuss both views and give your opinion
question:
Write about the following topic:

Some people believe that children should be taught to be competitive, while others think they should be taught to cooperate with others.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
answer:
Parents and educators often disagree about which values should be emphasised in a child's upbringing. Some believe that competition prepares young people for adult life, while others argue that cooperation is more important. In my view, both qualities are necessary, but cooperation should be the foundation on which healthy competition is built.

Those who favour competitiveness argue that the adult world is highly competitive. Students compete for places at universities, job applicants compete for positions, and companies compete for customers. Children who learn to compete from an early age, through sports, examinations or contests, may develop ambition, resilience and the motivation to improve their performance. Competition can also help them learn to cope with failure, an important lesson for later life.

On the other hand, supporters of cooperation emphasise that most achievements in modern society depend on teamwork. Scientific research, business projects and community initiatives all require people to share ideas, listen to others and work towards a common goal. Children who learn to cooperate develop empathy, communication skills and respect for different perspectives. Excessive competition, by contrast, may cause anxiety, damage self-esteem among children who rarely win, and encourage selfish behaviour or even dishonesty.

In my opinion, the most effective approach combines the two. Team sports offer a good example: players must cooperate closely with their teammates while competing against another team. Similarly, in the classroom, group projects can include an element of friendly competition between teams. In this way, children learn to strive for excellence without losing sight of the value of working with others.

In conclusion, while competition can motivate children, cooperation is essential for both personal wellbeing and social progress, and the two should be taught together.
